--- Page 1 ---
Lab 2: Working with Git Repositories
This lab is done in small groups of 2-3 people, so find your partners first.
If nobody around you is free, wave to a TA and they will pair you up.
What you will learn
Let your lab machine account talk to the hosting site for you
See how git keeps a history of your files
Practice the everyday git commands in the terminal
Rescue a file after you break it
Warm-up
Talk in your group about these questions:
Which book would you take to a desert island, and why?
What is a skill you learned this year that surprised you?
Take the two-minute check-in poll when you are done
PA1: begin early, work often
Every quarter the same advice shows up in the course notes.
--- Page 2 ---
Clone the repository
Use git clone with the repository link to copy the project onto your machine. The copy has the whole history, so you can look at any earlier commit.

Stage a change
Use git add followed by a file name to stage it. Staged files are what the next commit will record.

--- Page 6 ---
Push your work
Use git push to send your commits to the remote copy. If the push is rejected, pull first, fix any conflict and push again.
$ git commit -m "update notes"

Pull the latest
Run git pull to bring in commits your partner made. Git merges them with your own work and tells you when two edits touch the same lines.

Read the log
The command git log shows every commit with its author, date and message. Add --oneline for a compact list.
$ git status

--- Page 9 ---
Undo a destructive change
If you deleted a file by mistake, git restore brings back the last committed version. If you committed something you regret, git revert makes a new commit that cancels it.
$ git commit -m "update notes"
Question: Why does git ask for a message when you commit?

--- Page 10 ---
Branches
A branch is a movable name for a line of commits. Create one with git branch, switch with git switch and merge it back when the work is done.
$ git pull

--- Page 11 ---
Merge conflicts
When two people edit the same lines, git marks both versions in the file with arrows and equals signs. Edit the file to keep what you want, add it and commit.
Check: git status says the working tree is clean.
$ git switch -c fix-typo

--- Page 12 ---
Ignore generated files
List build products in a file called .gitignore so they never show up in git status. Compiled programs and object files do not belong in the repository.
